audit_findings.title: The OE anchor and current capital structure use incompatible interest economics
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 interest expense was $9.779m, including $8.615m of noncash debt-discount and issuance-cost amortization equal to 47.9% of the $18.0m OE anchor; normalized OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The expiring convertible-note interest expense reduces the equity-level OE anchor, while the bridge uses the post-refinancing cash and debt structure.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense was $9.8 million in 2025 and consisted of $8.6 million of amortization of debt discount and issuance costs and $1.2 million of interest incurred.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated period mismatch, not merely a possible risk. The June 2026 structure has $49.375m of term debt at a filed 4.16% effective rate, whereas FY2025 OE absorbed financing costs associated with $155.250m of convertible notes. Because the noncash amortization alone is nearly half the anchor, normalization could materially change operating value, although the exact after-tax adjustment requires a financing reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2026 contractual interest, fees, and amortization by instrument; remove the expired convertible-note amortization from the anchor, insert sustainable interest for the June 2026 debt structure, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Not all added cash may be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $99.711m is added in the bridge, equal to 28.2% of the $353.0m base equity value and $1.76 per diluted share; June 2026 deferred revenue was $36.116m; non-excess cash amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for customer advances or ordinary operating working capital should be excluded from the equity bridge rather than added as distributable excess cash.
audit_findings.evidence: Contract liabilities primarily relate to advance consideration received from customers (deferred revenue), for which transfer of control occurs, and therefore revenue is recognized as services are provided.
audit_findings.explanation: The full cash addition is demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much is operationally required. Deferred revenue shows that meaningful cash has been collected before related performance, but it is not automatically a dollar-for-dollar restriction on cash. The possible bridge reduction is therefore potentially important but presently unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Construct June 2026 net operating working capital by contract and liability category, establish a documented minimum operating-cash requirement, and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 tax expense may not represent sustainable cash taxes
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 cash taxes of $9.087m exceeded book tax expense of $2.813m by $6.274m, or 34.9% of the $18.0m OE anchor; the provision included a $12.389m current expense and $9.576m deferred benefit
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated sustainable tax charge inflates net-income-derived OE and therefore every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The income tax provision for 2025 was $2.8 million which yielded an effective tax rate of 24% compared to an income tax benefit of $4.2 million which yielded an effective tax rate of 461% in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 book-versus-cash difference is demonstrated and large relative to the anchor, although cash payments include timing effects and are not themselves a normalized tax measure. Nine-month FY2026 tax expense of $7.629m and cash taxes of $7.648m further show that FY2025's low net book provision should not be carried forward without reconciliation. The sustainable adjustment remains unresolved, but its plausible scale is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile current tax, deferred reversals, valuation-allowance releases, credits, R&D capitalization, and jurisdictional income; derive a sustainable cash-tax charge and rerun OE and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Patent indemnification exposure is an unquantified claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Defense costs, indemnification payments, settlements, royalties, or product restrictions could reduce cash in the bridge and/or future OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: However, the Company could incur substantial costs if it is determined that it is required to indemnify any customers or end-customers in connection with these offers or allegations.
audit_findings.explanation: The Candescent demand and underlying USAA litigation establish a live exposure, but not an accrued or estimable loss. The company disputes its indemnification obligation, and neither filing supplies a probability or loss range. This is therefore not a demonstrated valuation error, but the record cannot establish that the exposure is immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Obtain post-10-K case developments, the relevant indemnification agreements, insurance limits and exclusions, outside counsel's probability and loss-range assessment, and then apply any supported bridge deduction or probability-weighted OE impact.

audit_findings.title: Performance-award dilution has no verified maximum payout bound
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 outstanding Performance RSUs were 2.215780m target units, equal to 3.9% of the 56.750573m diluted-share denominator; incremental maximum shares unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Settlement above the units already included would increase the fully diluted share denominator and reduce value per share without reversing the retained SBC expense in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025, (i) 307,619 RSUs, (ii) 1,095,869 Performance RSUs, and (iii) stock options to purchase an aggregate of 45,000 shares of Common Stock were outstanding related to equity granted pursuant to inducement grants.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence and target quantity of the awards are filed, but no supplied evidence establishes their maximum settlement multiplier or confirms that the valuation denominator captures maximum payout. The known target units provide scale, but the incremental dilution and its materiality cannot be determined without the award terms.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every outstanding Performance RSU agreement and the latest proxy disclosures, calculate maximum issuable shares net of units already counted, and rerun value per share using the verified maximum denominator.

audit_findings.title: Estimated usage revenue can make the anchor depend on management forecasts
audit_findings.mechanism: Estimated usage above contractual minimums enters recognized revenue and net-income-derived OE before final billing and collection, potentially inflating the anchor and its projected growth base.
audit_findings.evidence: Usage above minimum commitment is estimated by looking at historical usage, expected volume, and other factors to project out for the remainder of the contract term.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting policy demonstrates that forecast usage can enter reported revenue, but the filings do not quantify the estimated component or show that prior estimates reversed or failed collection. This is therefore not a demonstrated overstatement. Because the affected amount and realization history are absent, materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain contract-level estimated-usage revenue included in FY2025, subsequent billings, collections, credits, and reversals; rerun the anchor using billed usage or a filed historically realized conversion rate.
